skill.name: pricing-strategy
skill.description: Design pricing, packaging, and monetization strategies based on value, customer willingness to pay, and growth objectives.
skill.summary: Design value-based pricing, packaging, and monetization strategies for growth-focused products.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged a Markdown value diagram and two pricing guidance lines, but context shows no executable command, system reconnaissance, or malicious intent. No semantic security findings or prompt-injection attempts were found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: Avoid “one price fits all” across fundamentally different buyers.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 64-72 are a fenced Markdown diagram showing value, price, alternatives, and cost. It contains no command syntax, interpreter call, or instruction to execute shell code.
Line 222 advises against a single price across different buyer segments. This is product pricing guidance, not host, network, or system reconnaissance.
Line 242 is a section heading for hybrid pricing models. It does not instruct the model to inspect the system or collect environment information.

content.value_statement: Pricing decisions often mix research, packaging, and revenue goals without a clear structure. This skill guides value metrics, tiers, price tests, and rollout plans.
actual_capabilities: Collects business model, market, performance, and pricing objective context.
Frames pricing around customer-perceived value and next best alternatives.
Explains pricing research methods such as Van Westendorp, conjoint, and Gabor-Granger.
Recommends value metrics and tier structures for different customer segments.
Compares freemium, free trial, and hybrid model tradeoffs.
Outlines price increase, testing, enterprise pricing, and rollout considerations.
limitations: It does not implement pricing pages or experiments directly.
It needs real customer, market, and performance inputs for reliable recommendations.
It provides strategy guidance, not legal, accounting, or financial advice.
It cannot prove demand or willingness to pay without external research.

use_cases.title: Launch a New Pricing Model
use_cases.description: Create an initial pricing structure using customer segments, value metrics, and competitive alternatives.

use_cases.title: Improve SaaS Packaging
use_cases.description: Redesign tiers so each plan maps to a clear buyer persona and upgrade path.

use_cases.title: Plan a Price Increase
use_cases.description: Assess signals, affected customers, rollout options, risks, and measurement needs before changing prices.

prompt_templates.title: Map Pricing Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure pricing for this product. Ask for any missing context about business model, target customers, alternatives, current pricing, and growth goals.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Value Metric
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate possible value metrics for my product. Compare user-based, usage-based, record-based, flat fee, and revenue-share options using customer value alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pricing Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a good, better, best tier structure for these personas. Explain included features, limits, upgrade triggers, and pricing rationale for each tier.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Pricing Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess a proposed price increase. Identify affected segments, expected impact, research needed, rollout path, communication risks, and success metrics.

output_examples.input: A B2B SaaS tool wants to move from one flat plan to tiered pricing.
output: Recommended tiers: entry plan for small teams, core plan for active teams, and enterprise plan for security needs.
Primary value metric: seats, with usage limits to support expansion.
Key risk: current customers may resist feature movement without clear migration messaging.

output_examples.input: A marketplace wants to evaluate whether revenue share fits its pricing.
output: Revenue share aligns with customer outcomes when transactions are measurable and trusted.
A platform fee may be needed if fixed operating costs are high.
Test willingness to pay across seller sizes before changing the model.

output_examples.input: A product team wants to increase prices for new customers.
output: Use new-customer pricing first to reduce disruption for existing accounts.
Track conversion, win rate, churn, expansion, and sales-cycle changes.
Prepare a migration policy before extending changes to existing customers.

best_practices: Anchor every price recommendation to customer-perceived value and next best alternatives.
Separate packaging decisions from price-level decisions before choosing final numbers.
Validate major changes with customer research, sales feedback, and clear success metrics.
anti_patterns: Using internal cost as the main pricing basis when customer value is measurable.
Applying one price to buyer segments with different budgets, needs, and usage levels.
Running surprise price tests that damage trust or confuse active buyers.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create pricing strategy documents, tier structures, value metric recommendations, and pricing change plans.

faq.question: Can it choose exact prices for my product?
faq.answer: It can recommend price ranges and rationale, but exact prices need customer research and market validation.

faq.question: Does it work for SaaS products?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SaaS pricing patterns such as seats, usage, tier packaging, freemium, trials, and enterprise plans.

faq.question: Can it help with price increases?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers signals for increases, rollout options, customer impact, risks, and measurement plans.

faq.question: Does it build pricing pages?
faq.answer: No. It defines the pricing strategy, but implementation and page conversion work belong in separate workflows.

faq.question: What inputs improve the output?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include customer segments, current pricing, competitors, value delivered, conversion, churn, and revenue goals.
